correctness.rationale: For all v,D,alpha,r>0 and eta in [0,1], apply the explicitly written Markov generator to y,s,ys,y². Fair invariant sign balance gives reset source r/2 for each sign independent of eta. These yield EYS=v/(r+2alpha) and EY²=2D/r+2v²/[r(r+2alpha)]. Conditional semigroup regression gives C_eta(t)=V exp(-rt)+[v²/(r+2alpha)] times the positive exponential convolution exactly for every t≥0. Strict positivity of the integrand difference for eta1<eta2 at t>0 proves monotonicity; elementary positive-leading-term cases prove slowest-rate and resonant t exp(-rt) behavior; Tonelli proves integrated covariance. Independently implemented checker.py passed 1080 generator semigroup comparisons, nine Fourier resolvent comparisons, and three 100000-sample stationary event-driven covariance tests. These finite checks are corroboration, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Already-known η-independence of the stationary state poses a natural experimentally relevant identifiability gap. The all-lag theorem shows strict protocol differentiation invisible to all one-time observations, a single-lag identifiability theorem (when other parameters are known), and a complete nontrivial orientation-memory to reset-memory relaxation crossover at eta_c=1/2-alpha/r with a resonant t exp(-rt) boundary, plus a Green–Kubo integral. These distinguish dynamic behavior of physically identical stationary ensembles, rather than computing an arbitrary finite parameter slice. No independent audit or broad universality claim is made.
